narrative_purpose: Shows the setting where polymerisation actually works: a volcanic shore whose pools stand at different stages of drying, under the eclipse light that gives Pandora more wet-dry cycles than Earth gets.
subject: A rocky volcanic shoreline of dark fractured basalt, holding perhaps seven shallow rounded pools of different sizes. Some pools are brim-full of still water; others are half-empty with wide pale mineral crusts ringing their inner edges in concentric rims; two are almost dry, their floors showing cracked pale residue. Low gentle surf reaches the outer rocks at the far left. Above, an enormous banded gas giant sits low in the sky directly in front of the star, its dark disc rimmed by a thin bright ring of light where the star is hidden behind it.
scene: A volcanic coast at the moment of eclipse, the landscape in deep dim shadow with only the rim light and faint reflected glow illuminating it, low dark hills behind the shoreline.
camera: A slightly elevated three-quarter view looking down and across the pools toward the water and the eclipsed sky beyond.
light: Very low overall. A thin ring of pale amber light around the gas giant's dark disc is the brightest thing in frame, casting a weak warm sheen along the wet pool surfaces and the surf; everything else falls into deep indigo shadow. The dry pool crusts catch a faint cool highlight.
palette: Void-indigo and deep teal-indigo rock and shadow dominating, pale stone mineral crusts, a single restrained warm ember-amber accent in the eclipse rim and its reflections on the water.
style: Painterly speculative-biology landscape plate, hand-painted rock texture, naturalist observation rather than dramatic vista.
detail_level: Crisp on the near pools, their mineral rims and cracked dry floors; softening through the middle distance into haze; the gas giant kept soft and low-contrast.
composition: Pools arranged across the lower two thirds from full at the left to nearly dry at the right so the drying sequence reads left to right, the eclipsed gas giant low in the upper right, dark sky and hillside kept plain for overlaid callouts.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette with the eclipse rim as the only warm accent. The pools must clearly differ in water level with visible concentric mineral rims marking former levels — that gradient is the figure's teaching content. Nothing alive anywhere in frame.
